title: continuous-batching-scheduler-tuning-experiments-10
content:
Summary:
This doc captures the latest continuous-batching scheduler tuning experiments (run: Feb 2024) focused on how batch_size, queue timeout, and fairness policies impact p50/p95/p99 latency, tail behavior, and throughput for typical conversational workloads. Goal: find a default config that minimizes p95/p99 without regressing p50 or throughput for interactive workloads while preserving fairness across request size classes.

Environment:
- Cluster: dev-serving-pool-a (2x A100-40GB per node), 8 nodes used for experiments
- Runtime: serving-runtime v2.7.1-experiments branch (profiling hooks enabled)
- Workloads: mix of short (prompt tokens ~50, response tokens ~20) and long (prompt ~600, response ~400) requests to mirror chat + long completion usage. Traffic replay derived from production traces (Jan 2024, anonymized).
- Load generator: custom harness (github PR above) replaying 1.2x baseline qps to reveal tail behavior.
- Metrics captured: request_count, tokens_generated, qps, cpu_gpu_util, batch_size_observed, p50/p95/p99 latency (inference-only and end-to-end), 99.9th tail, drop_rate, fairness_skew (difference in median latency across size classes).

Methodology:
- Sweep variables: max_batch_size (4, 8, 16, 32, 48), queue_timeout_ms (5, 10, 20, 50, 100, 200), fairness_mode (fifo, age_based, size_aware).
- Each experiment run: 30m warmup + 60m measurement window. 3 runs per config; reported values are median across runs.
- Profiling: NVTX ranges + kernel timelines for 10% sample. Scheduler internals traced for batching events (batch creation time, oldest_request_age, dropped_by_timeout).

Key findings (high-level):
1) Increasing max_batch_size helps throughput but worsens p99 for short requests unless queue_timeout_ms is reduced.
2) Very small timeouts (<=5ms) reduce p99 for short requests but harm throughput and increase GPU underutilization for power-law long-request mixes.
3) Age-based fairness significantly reduces tail latency skew across short/long classes compared to FIFO at modest throughput levels; cost is a small p50 regression (~3-6ms) for long requests.
4) Size-aware batching (grouping by request prompt length) gave best tradeoff in mixed workloads, reducing cross-class interference and improving overall p99 while keeping throughput within 2-4% of max.

Selected detailed results (aggregated):
- Baseline (max_batch=32, timeout=50ms, fifo):
  - qps: 125 (tokens/sec normalized)
  - gpu_util: 92%
  - p50: 42ms, p95: 210ms, p99: 840ms, p999: 1.9s
  - fairness_skew (median short vs long): 420ms

- Config A (max_batch=16, timeout=20ms, age_based):
  - qps: 118 (-6%)
  - gpu_util: 88%
  - p50: 44ms, p95: 160ms, p99: 420ms, p999: 1.05s
  - fairness_skew: 160ms
  - Notes: dramatic p99 improvement for short requests; kernel timelines show fewer long-running KV-cache stalls caused by large mixed batches.

- Config B (max_batch=32, timeout=10ms, size_aware grouping into small/large queues, fifo per-queue):
  - qps: 122 (-2%)
  - gpu_util: 90%
  - p50: 43ms, p95: 145ms, p99: 360ms, p999: 780ms
  - fairness_skew: 95ms
  - Notes: best overall p95/p99 with minimal throughput loss. Observed batch composition more homogeneous; average observed batch_size for small queue was 8, for large queue 18.

- Config C (max_batch=48, timeout=100ms, fifo):
  - qps: 133 (+6%)
  - gpu_util: 96%
  - p50: 40ms, p95: 250ms, p99: 1.1s, p999: 2.6s
  - fairness_skew: 720ms
  - Notes: high throughput but severe tail for short requests due to head-of-line blocking by long requests. Not acceptable for interactive SLAs.

Profiling notes / bottlenecks observed:
- KV cache eviction and reload (cache misses) were frequent when large mixed batches included long sequences; time spent in memory copies and attention kernel setup increased. Reducing cross-size mixing (size_aware) reduced these stalls.
- Scheduler overhead: median scheduling overhead ~0.8ms, but 99th scheduling overhead climbed to ~12ms when queue_timeout_ms was high and max_batch_size large (scheduler searching to fill a large batch while waiting caused queue churn).
- Backend saturation: when max_batch_size>=32 and timeout>=50ms, kernel launch queues experienced bursty peaks that pushed p999 up.

Fairness experiments summary:
- FIFO: simplest, best throughput at high batches, worst for short-request tail.
- Age-based: prioritizes older requests; reduces starvation of short requests when long requests pile up, helps p99 significantly; can slightly reduce throughput because it sometimes fires suboptimal (not fully packed) batches.
- Size-aware: partitioning queues by request size gave the best balance for mixed workloads; requires heuristic thresholds (we used small: <=128 prompt tokens, large: >128) and slightly more scheduler complexity.

Recommendations / Proposed default config for interactive workloads (mixed short+long):
- Default: size_aware queues with max_batch_size_global = 32, per-queue soft_max: small=16, large=32, queue_timeout_ms = 10ms, fairness=fifo-per-queue + age_preemption across queues (age threshold 40ms).
  - Rationale: keeps p95/p99 low for short requests while preserving most throughput for long requests.
- For latency-sensitive tiers (paid real-time): reduce global max_batch_size to 16 and timeout to 5-10ms, enable age_based across all queues.
- For throughput/batch jobs: increase max_batch_size to 48 and timeout to 100ms, FIFO acceptable.

Action items / follow-ups:
- (Ava) Implement size-aware partitioning as a first-class scheduler mode (PR in progress: see linked PR).
- (Ravi) Add microbench marks isolating KV-cache reload cost vs batch composition (ticket SERVE-1301).
- (Jordan) Run a longer 24h stability run with proposed default to capture rare tail (p9999) events and memory growth.
- Add telemetry: per-batch composition histogram, per-request oldest_request_age metric, and per-queue tail-latency alerts.

Appendix: quick tips for reproducing runs
- Checkout branch: serving-runtime:experiments/continuous-batching-2024
- Deploy to dev-serving-pool-a with 8 nodes; use experiment harness config in /infra/bench/continuous-batch-config.yaml
- Use load generator flag --preserve-size-distribution to keep mixed workloads representative of production

Notes (informal):
- We saw a handful of anomalous p999 spikes correlating with concurrent infra jobs (checkpointing) — need isolation in next runs.
- Some config combinations (very low timeout + large max_batch) produced frequent tiny batches, driving up kernel launch overhead; we should add a minimum effective_batch_size heuristic to prevent pathological config pairs.

End of doc.
